text:
maya: Heads-up — StellarAI POC is hitting intermittent 429s during bulk embeddings test. Starts ~45s into a 5-worker run. They're on a trial key with per-route credits. Can we triage?

sam: Can you paste the failing response headers (X-RateLimit etc) and one `curl -v` (with X-Request-ID) if possible? Any client-side retries?

maya: Paste from their capture: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1718932500` and we also saw `x-redeemed-route-credit: 0`. They said they retried aggressively.

kevin: Hmm, that reset looks like minute-bucket exhaustion. Are we sure the test is measured in tokens/min not qps? Lia, can you check the route credit mapping for their tenant? @lia

lia: Looking — trial tenants get a shared embeddings pool by default, but this tenant had a per-route override that pointed to a small dedicated bucket (probably a provisioning race). Also their batch size jumped mid-run so token-per-request spiked.

sam: Ask them to re-run one failing request with `curl -v` and paste the `X-Request-ID`. Also request client-side logs showing retry timing — if they retry immediately it will exhaust the minute bucket faster.

maya: Customer logs: spike to ~600 tokens/sec per worker then 429, no backoff. Their embedding batch size auto-increased from 8 -> 32 during run.

quota-bot: Auto-notice: Tenant t-stellar state=THROTTLED; per-route softcap reached (embeddings) 500/min. Suggested temporary bump +200/min for 2h.

kevin: Ok — root cause = token/min softcap + per-route bucket misassignment + client retries. Plan: apply temp bump to stop immediate failures, then fix provisioning logic and docs. I can do the bump.

lia: Also recommend client changes: jittered start times across workers and exponential backoff on 429. We should add a warning in onboarding about variable token footprint for embeddings and how minute buckets behave.

maya: Requested temp bump and told customer: "We've increased your minute token cap by +200 for 2 hours. Please retry with 3 concurrent workers and enable jittered backoff; share X-Request-ID if you still hit 429." Will report back.

sam: After bump — customer reports a 10-minute run with no 429s. They reduced concurrency and added jitter.

kevin: Follow-ups: (1) create infra ticket to ensure per-route overrides don't point to undersized buckets during provisioning, (2) change trial defaults to larger embedding buckets, (3) add telemetry to surface token/min pressure in Console.

lia: I'll update the POC playbook with recommended client configs (batch sizing, jitter, backoff, token estimate examples) and add a short checklist for sales pre-checks.

maya: Thanks all — customer happy for now. :tada:
